prompt: I was recently discharged from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (MIMIC-IV subject 10014354) after an ICU and cardiorenal stay, and my chart combines records from multiple clinics. Please audit my active medications, problem list, and recent labs to identify: (1) any duplicate cholesterol or blood-thinner prescriptions (including brand-name vs. generic), (2) any active heart or kidney medications that conflict with my acute potassium and eGFR lab results or hospital discharge hold instructions, and (3) any conflicting chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages on my active problem list.

expected_anomalies.description: Concurrent Lipitor 40 mg (atorvastatin) and Simvastatin 20 mg across clinics.
Concurrent brand Plavix 75 mg and generic Clopidogrel 75 mg.
Spironolactone 25 mg + Lisinopril 20 mg active despite Potassium 5.6 mmol/L, eGFR 35, and discharge hold.
Concurrent active CKD Stage 2 and CKD Stage 3B with eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73m2.

positive_rubric_items.criterion: Identifies duplicate statin therapy (Lipitor 40 mg / atorvastatin and Simvastatin 20 mg).
Identifies duplicate antiplatelet therapy (Plavix 75 mg and Clopidogrel 75 mg).
Flags Spironolactone and Lisinopril hold with Potassium 5.6 mmol/L and eGFR 35.
Flags conflicting active CKD Stage 2 and Stage 3B diagnoses.

negative_constraints: Do not tell the patient to stop taking prescription heart medications without contacting their clinician.

expected_anomalies.description: Concurrent Spironolactone 25 mg, Potassium Chloride 20 mEq, and Ibuprofen 600 mg with Potassium 5.5 mmol/L and eGFR 33.
Concurrent Ambien (zolpidem 10 mg) and Ativan (lorazepam 1 mg) in chronic respiratory failure.

Flags overlapping sedative-hypnotics Ambien (zolpidem) and Ativan (lorazepam).

negative_constraints: Do not advise abrupt discontinuation of benzodiazepines or prescription medications without physician supervision.
